title: Studio 'Evidence & proof' drawer shows '0 events' and six empty tabs after a completed sample/replay session, contradicting the 16-event hash-chained proof record downloadable from the same page
reproducibility: deterministic in sample and replay modes
route: /session/<uuid>, /proof/<uuid>, /replay/leakage-01 (bottom drawer, all tabs: Activity, Plan, Diff, Tests, Verifier, Provenance)
journey: judge 10-minute test; any judge who opens the transparency drawer
environment: browser audit 2026-07-19, sample session session_8fca6bad-b3dd-4469-9f66-e4f7637916c4 and replay leakage-01
prerequisites: complete the sample lesson (or walk the replay) to the proof screen
steps: From /judge click 'Start sample' and complete the loop to /proof/<uuid>
Click 'Evidence & proof · 0 events · Open' in the bottom drawer
Open each tab: Activity, Plan, Diff, Tests, Verifier, Provenance
expected: Drawer lists the session's plan, diff, test, verifier and provenance evidence — at minimum the same 16-event chain contained in the downloadable proof record, or an explicit note that telemetry is live-mode-only with a link to the capsule
actual: Counter reads '0 events'; every tab shows an empty state ('No activity evidence yet. It will appear here when the session produces it.', 'No plan evidence yet.', 'No verifier evidence yet.') while the downloadable proof record from the same page contains 16 hash-chained events including codex and verifier entries

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: Observed empty drawer across all six tabs in completed sample session and in replay mode

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: Downloaded proof record for the identical session contains 16 events (session.created through patch.verified; actors system/learner/codex/verifier/kernel)

likely_cause: drawer feed is wired only to live-pipeline telemetry (or an event endpoint not populated for bundled/replayed sessions) and the empty-state copy was written for in-progress sessions
unverified: whether the drawer populates correctly for live sessions (could not upload a notebook in the browser)
learner_impact: low for learning itself; learners are told evidence exists that the app then appears to deny
judge_impact: high — a judge's natural 'show me the telemetry' click returns '0 events', making the flagship evidence-chain claim look like marketing at the exact moment of evaluation
trust_impact: high — direct, visible contradiction of the core differentiator
recommended_correction: Populate the drawer from the session event chain for all modes (sample and replay already possess one), including codex compilation and verifier entries; badge entries with their mode
smallest_correction: Change the empty state to link the truth: 'This session's signed event chain (16 events) is available in the downloadable proof record below' with an anchor to the download
acceptance_criteria: After completing sample and replay, the drawer event count matches the capsule event count and at least Activity/Verifier/Provenance tabs render entries; empty-state copy never claims no evidence exists when a capsule does
regression_test: e2e: complete sample lesson -> assert drawer counter == proof record events length; assert each tab renders >=1 entry or an explicit mode-scoped explanation
dependencies: event feed endpoint for non-live modes

title: Transfer gate polarity contradiction: top instruction and check-mark icon direct the learner to the safe feature ('Known item price — uses available information ✓'), but the gate only passes when selecting the leaky feature ('Centered rolling target', marked ×) as the answer to 'Which feature crosses NOW?'
reproducibility: reproduced twice failing with the ✓-marked option, then passing with the ×-marked option; corroborated in the session event log (transfer.failed x2, then transfer.passed with identifiedRisks=['centered_window_reads_future'])
route: /session/<uuid> step 5 Apply (also present in /replay/leakage-01 transfer step)
journey: judge 3-minute story walk; learner sample lesson
user: judge speed-running the demo; first-time learner
environment: browser audit 2026-07-19, sample session and replay
prerequisites: reach step 5 Apply in the sample lesson
steps: At the transfer task read the instruction: 'Choose the split and feature that match what is available when a real prediction is made'
Select 'Time-ordered holdout' (split) and 'Known item price' (feature) — the option the timeline marks with ✓ 'uses available information'
Click 'Check transfer' -> observe 'Transfer not yet passed… The patch remains locked'
Repeat identical selection -> fails again
Select 'Centered rolling target' (marked × 'reads later outcomes') -> click 'Check transfer' -> passes and unlocks the patch
expected: Instruction, per-option affordances, and acceptance logic share one polarity: either the task is 'choose the deployment-safe split and feature' (then Known item price must pass) or 'identify the split that respects time and the feature that crosses NOW' (then the instruction and the ✓/× icons must say so)
actual: Mixed polarity: split question is choose-the-good-one, feature question is identify-the-bad-one; the ✓ icon sits on the option that fails the gate and the × icon on the option that passes it; error text ('remove any feature that reads values to the right of NOW') is the only correct signpost

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: Two failed checks with Time-ordered holdout + Known item price; pass with Time-ordered holdout + Centered rolling target

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: proof record events 9-12 transfer.failed, events 13-14 transfer.passed with identifiedRisks=['centered_window_reads_future']

likely_cause: the feature panel was re-authored as a risk-identification question ('Which feature crosses NOW?') without updating the task-level instruction and the per-selection ✓/× feedback, which still teach choose-the-safe-feature
unverified: whether failure-then-success is an intended 'productive struggle' design (if so, the ✓ icon is still actively misleading)
learner_impact: medium — blocks the Repair unlock (the pedagogical payoff) and teaches the wrong signal: the UI rewards with ✓ an answer the system grades as wrong
judge_impact: medium-high — a judge following the app's own green check gets 'Transfer not yet passed' twice during the flagship 3-minute story; reads as a bug, not pedagogy
trust_impact: medium — invites the question 'is the gate grading anything coherent?'
recommended_correction: Unify polarity: keep the gate as risk-identification; rewrite the task instruction to 'Choose the evaluation that matches deployment, and identify the feature that crosses the NOW line'; render the ✓/× as neutral property tags ('safe at prediction time' / 'reads the future') not selection feedback
smallest_correction: Change the top instruction sentence to mirror the two sub-questions exactly, and remove the ✓ glyph next to 'Known item price uses available information' (replace with a neutral info dot)
acceptance_criteria: A first-time user selecting the UI's visually-endorsed options passes the gate on the first attempt; instruction text and grading key verified consistent by content review
regression_test: e2e matrix over all four split x feature combinations asserting pass only for (time-ordered, centered-rolling-target) and asserting no ✓ affordance appears on failing options
effort: S (copy + icon change) to M (if gate semantics change)

title: Legacy replay shows perpetual 'Preparing proof' spinner and disabled 'Download proof record'/'Download repaired notebook' buttons with no explanation; /judge's 'legacy v1 replay does not offer a Proof Capsule' disclosure is never repeated in-app
category: stale-state / confusing live-vs-replay behaviour / missing copy
prerequisites: walk the replay to completion (requires re-solving the interactive transfer gate)
steps: Open /replay/leakage-01, continue to the result, complete the transfer gate, click 'Verify notebook patch'
Observe the Reasoning Diff card header: 'Preparing proof' disabled button
Observe 'Download repaired notebook' and 'Download proof record' rendered but disabled
Wait across multiple interactions: state never resolves
expected: A terminal, explained state: 'Proof Capsule unavailable for this legacy v1 recording (2026-07-14). Run the sample lesson or a live session to generate a signed capsule.' Buttons either hidden or disabled with that reason attached
actual: 'Preparing proof' spins forever (a loading state that never resolves), both download buttons are greyed out with no tooltip or reason; the only place the v1 limitation is disclosed is back on /judge

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: perpetual 'Preparing proof' + disabled downloads at replay end; persisted across interactions and revisit

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: /judge replay card text: 'This legacy v1 replay is genuine but does not offer a Proof Capsule download'

likely_cause: replay final screen reuses the live proof panel whose async preparation never completes for v1 recordings; no terminal 'unavailable' state was designed
unverified: whether 'Preparing proof' ever resolves on very long waits (observed ~2 minutes across interactions)
judge_impact: medium-high — the replay is the fastest judge path; ending it on what looks like a hung loader undercuts the flagship Proof Capsule claim precisely where a judge checks it
recommended_correction: Introduce an explicit terminal state for legacy replays explaining the v1 limitation and offering the sample lesson as the capsule-generating path
smallest_correction: Replace the spinner label with 'Proof Capsule unavailable for this 2026-07-14 v1 recording' and add a one-line reason under the disabled buttons
acceptance_criteria: No indefinite loading state anywhere in replay; the v1 limitation is stated on the replay final screen itself; a judge never needs to return to /judge to understand why downloads are disabled
regression_test: e2e: finish replay -> assert no element with loading state remains; assert explanatory text present; assert buttons either hidden or disabled with accessible reason
score_leverage: medium-high (Design; converts an apparent bug into disclosed honesty)

title: Unexplained dual result hashes for replay_id leakage-01: legacy replay displays 2501654264b9…, fresh sample sessions display a6ae7652e04e… with identical metrics/seed; both hashes coexist unlabelled in the v2 capsule, and the replay banner commit (4f2f6472…, 40 hex) differs from lab.verified commitHash (1050fa76…, 32 hex)
reproducibility: deterministic; corroborated across two independent sample sessions (this audit's and Agent 2's proof records)
environment: browser audit 2026-07-19; local JSON analysis of two capsules from different sessions
prerequisites: view replay result hash; complete a sample session and download its proof record
steps: Note result hash 2501654264b9… on the replay result panel
Complete a fresh sample session; note result hash a6ae7652e04e… (same metrics: 98.5/59.4/67.4%, seed 1729, 389/0 overlap)

Download the proof record; observe events[5] verifier lab.verified carries resultHash 2501654264b9… recordedAt 2026-07-14, while events[6] kernel experiment.completed and verifiedResultSet carry a6ae7652e04e…
Compare commit identifiers: replay banner 'Commit 4f2f647228304d63ac8b9cba8cdca1dc7a07e192' vs lab.verified commitHash '1050fa76b9e7b759bf6cd56d1f0d789f67e8f1c8'
expected: One canonical result hash per replay_id, or an explicit lineage label ('v1 recorded hash' vs 'v2 recomputed hash — hash schema changed; metrics identical') and consistent commit identifiers
actual: Two different 'verified' result hashes for the same experiment identity with no explanation anywhere; the external verifier's 'canonical_result_hash' invariant corresponds to the v1 recording while the UI and verifiedResultSet present the v2 value; two unrelated commit identifiers

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: hash values captured in-app from replay and sample session result panels

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: events[5].payload.resultHash=2501654264b9… (recordedAt 2026-07-14T11:18:03Z) vs events[6].payload.resultHash=a6ae7652e04e… in the same bundle

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: identical dual-hash pattern in Agent 2's independent session capsule (session_db9778ae)

likely_cause: v1->v2 hash-schema or payload-serialization change made fresh recomputation produce a different digest over identical metrics; the v2 capsule embeds the v1 recorded verification evidence without lineage annotation; commit identifiers come from two different sources (git SHA vs content hash)
unverified: exact serialization cause (no repo access from the web surface)
judge_impact: medium — most judges won't diff hashes, but the one who does (the technical judge this product is built to impress) finds the 'canonical_result_hash' claim internally inconsistent
trust_impact: high for verifier-minded evaluators; it is exactly the class of contradiction CounterLab exists to catch
recommended_correction: Add explicit lineage: label the 2026-07-14 recorded hash as the v1 canonical reference, the fresh hash as the v2 recomputation, state why they differ (schema version), and unify commit identifiers; include the mapping in the capsule's limitations/versions block
smallest_correction: One sentence on the replay and proof screens: 'Result hash schema upgraded after this v1 recording; metrics are byte-identical (98.5/59.4/67.4, seed 1729)'
acceptance_criteria: Every surface that shows a result hash identifies its schema/version; capsule contains an explicit supersedes/recorded-vs-recomputed field; replay banner and lab.verified use the same commit identifier or explain the two formats
regression_test: unit/e2e: sample capsule must contain a lineage field linking recorded and recomputed hashes; UI snapshot asserts hash labels
dependencies: none for copy; schema field for full fix
score_leverage: high for Technological Implementation credibility; low cost

Click 'Continue with my notebook →'
Observe artifact card: 'LOADING / Preparing artifact… / Support decision: Pending' with no upload prompt

evidence.label: Directly observed

title: Proof-capsule HMAC signature is not independently verifiable by a judge (symmetric key server-side; no public verify endpoint or key publication)
steps: Inspect integrity block: mode hmac-signed, algorithm hmac-sha256, contentHash, eventChainHead, signature
Look for a public verification endpoint or key — none exists on-site
expected: Either asymmetric signatures, a public /verify endpoint accepting a capsule upload, or explicit scoping of what the signature proves (server-self-attestation)
actual: Only internal consistency (hash chain) is checkable; the signature's authenticity is unverifiable without server cooperation. Mitigation present: capsule limitations already concede 'Docker enforcement is evidence for this local run, not a formal sandbox proof'

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: integrity block fields

likely_cause: HMAC chosen for integrity/attestation simplicity; no public verification surface built
unverified: whether a verify endpoint exists outside the sitemap
judge_impact: low-medium — only the deepest technical judges reach this
trust_impact: medium for that audience; the honest limitations blunt it
recommended_correction: Ship a /verify endpoint (or signed-by-publishable-key scheme) and link it from the capsule and /judge
smallest_correction: One limitation line: 'The HMAC signature attests server-side integrity; independent verification requires the repository verifier'
acceptance_criteria: A judge can verify a downloaded capsule without private keys, or the limitation is explicitly stated wherever the signature is mentioned
regression_test: e2e: upload tampered capsule to /verify → rejected
